records.name: Tokyo Skytree
records.description: A 634-meter broadcasting tower in Oshiage that is the tallest tower in the world and the tallest structure in Japan. Two observation decks, Tembo Deck at 350m and Tembo Galleria at 450m, offer panoramic views over Tokyo that can extend to Mt. Fuji on clear days. It opened in May 2012.

tips.text: Last entry to the observation decks is 60 minutes before closing.

records.hours: 10:00-22:00 on weekdays, 9:00-22:00 on weekends and holidays (last entry 60 minutes before closing; varies seasonally)
records.station: Tokyo Skytree Station (Tobu Skytree Line) or Oshiage Station, both about 1 minute on foot

records.name: Tokyo Skytree Town
records.description: A multipurpose complex at the base of Tokyo Skytree that opened in 2012. It includes the Tokyo Solamachi shopping and dining arcade, Sumida Aquarium, and a planetarium, combining modern attractions with the surrounding shitamachi neighborhood character.
records.station: Tokyo Skytree Station (Tobu Skytree Line) or Oshiage Station, both about 1 minute on foot

records.name: Sumida Aquarium
records.description: A public aquarium on the 5th and 6th floors of Tokyo Skytree Town that opened alongside the tower in May 2012. It uses artificial seawater in all tanks and houses roughly 7,000 animals across 260 species, including an Ogasawara Islands fish tank, a Magellanic penguin pool, and a large goldfish display called the Edorium.
records.station: Tokyo Skytree Station
records.address: 1-1-2 Oshiage, Sumida City, Tokyo (Tokyo Skytree Town)

records.name: Ryogoku Kokugikan
records.description: Tokyo's national sumo arena, seating about 11,098 spectators. Opened in January 1985 to replace the older Kuramae Kokugikan, it hosts three of the six annual grand sumo tournaments (January, May, September) and also stages boxing, professional wrestling, and other events. The Sumo Museum occupies its first floor.
records.station: Ryogoku Station (JR Chuo-Sobu Line and Toei Oedo Line)

records.name: Sumo Museum
records.description: A museum inside Ryogoku Kokugikan holding roughly 30,000-40,000 sumo-related items, including woodblock prints, ceremonial aprons (keshō-mawashi), and rank sheets (banzuke). Founded in 1954 from the private collection of Count Tadamasa Sakai, it moved to its current location inside the arena in 1985 and runs rotating exhibitions rather than a permanent display.

tips.text: Admission is generally free, except during Tokyo tournament days when a spectator ticket to the sumo hall is required.

records.station: Ryogoku Station (JR Chuo-Sobu Line and Toei Oedo Line)
records.address: Inside Ryogoku Kokugikan, Sumida City, Tokyo

records.name: Edo-Tokyo Museum
records.description: A history museum in Ryogoku covering Tokyo's development from 1590 onward, with a life-size replica of Nihonbashi bridge and scale models spanning the Edo, Meiji, and Showa periods. Designed by architect Kiyonori Kikutake and opened in 1993, it closed in April 2022 for its first major renovation and reopened on March 31, 2026.
records.station: Ryogoku Station

records.name: Sumida Hokusai Museum
records.description: A museum dedicated to ukiyo-e artist Katsushika Hokusai, who was born in Sumida. It opened in November 2016 in a building designed by Pritzker Prize-winning architect Kazuyo Sejima of SANAA, with five interlocking aluminum-clad volumes. The collection holds more than 1,800 items including paintings, sketches, woodblock prints, and personal artifacts.

tips.text: Last entry is 30 minutes before closing.

records.hours: 9:30-17:30, Tuesday-Sunday and holidays (last entry 30 minutes before closing); closed Mondays and New Year's holidays
records.station: Ryogoku Station (5 minutes via Toei Oedo Line, 9 minutes via JR Sobu Line)

records.name: Kyu-Yasuda Teien (Former Yasuda Garden)
records.description: A former samurai residence garden dating to 1691, near Ryogoku Kokugikan. Its pond was once tide-fed by the Sumida River; pumps now raise and lower the water level to recreate that effect. The estate passed to Yasuda Zenjiro and was donated to the public after his death in 1922, then restored and reopened as a park by 1927 following Great Kanto Earthquake damage. Admission is free.
records.hours: 9:00-19:30 (seasonally shortened to 9:00-18:00); closed New Year's holidays
records.station: Ryogoku Station (JR Sobu Line / Toei Oedo Line), 5 minutes on foot

records.name: Mukojima-Hyakkaen Gardens
records.description: An Edo-period flower garden created in 1804 by antiques dealer Sahara Kiku, who planted 360 plum trees; its name means 'a garden with a hundred flowers blooming through the four seasons.' It is the only surviving flower garden from the Edo period, known for stones inscribed with poetry by notable figures of the era. Nationally designated a Place of Scenic Beauty in 1933, it was destroyed in World War II and restored by 1949.

tips.text: Last entry is 30 minutes before closing.

records.hours: 9:00-17:00 daily (last entry 30 minutes before closing); closed December 29-January 3
records.station: Higashi-Mukojima Station (Tobu Skytree Line), 8-minute walk

records.name: Ekoin Temple
records.description: A Jodo-shu Buddhist temple formally named Shoshuzan Muen-ji Ekoin, founded in 1657 by the fourth Tokugawa shogun to honor roughly 100,000 victims of the Great Meireki Fire. It later became a major sumo venue, hosting charity tournaments from 1768 and continuous tournaments from 1833 to 1909, a period known as 'Ekoin sumo.' The grounds include the Chikara-zuka mound, where apprentice wrestlers pray for strength.
records.station: Ryogoku Station (JR Sobu Line, West Exit), 3-minute walk

records.name: Yokoamicho Park (Tokyo Metropolitan Memorial Hall)
records.description: A park on the former site of the Honjo Army Clothing Depot, which became a refuge site during the 1923 Great Kanto Earthquake. It contains the Tokyo Metropolitan Memorial Hall, designed by Ito Chuta, which honors victims of the earthquake and the 1945 Tokyo air raids, and the Memorial Hall of Reconstruction, which displays related artifacts. Admission is free.
records.hours: 9:00-16:30 daily (Memorial Hall); closed New Year's holidays
records.station: Ryogoku Station (Toei Oedo Line, Exit A1), 2-minute walk

records.name: Ushijima Shrine
records.description: A Shinto shrine next to Sumida Park on the east bank of the Sumida River, said to have been built in 860. Its name references cattle grazing once done in the area, and the shrine is known for a bronze 'rubbing ox' statue that visitors touch for healing. It was one of the local scenes depicted by ukiyo-e artist Katsushika Hokusai.

records.name: Mimeguri Shrine
records.description: A Shinto shrine in the Mukojima area on the east bank of the Sumida River. It is one of the Edo-period riverside sites that ukiyo-e artist Katsushika Hokusai, who lived most of his life in Sumida, depicted in his prints.

records.name: Japanese Sword Museum
records.description: A small museum operated by the Society for the Preservation of Japanese Art Swords, dedicated to Japanese swordmaking. It displays about 190 items including katana, sword mountings, and armor, some designated national treasures or important cultural properties. The current building near Ryogoku opened in January 2018, replacing a previous location that closed in March 2017.
records.station: Ryogoku Station

records.name: Tobacco and Salt Museum
records.description: A museum run by Japan Tobacco covering the history of tobacco and salt in Japan and abroad. Established in 1978, originally in Shibuya, it relocated to its current Sumida location in 2015. The collection holds about 38,000 items, including a large block of Polish rock salt and a replica Mayan shrine.

records.name: Tobu Museum
records.description: A railway and transport museum operated by Tobu Railway, opened in May 1989 to mark the company's 90th anniversary. It displays historic Tobu trains and buses, including the company's first steam locomotive and first electric train and locomotive.
records.station: Higashi-Mukojima Station

records.name: TOKYO mizumachi / Sumida River Walk
records.description: A waterfront pedestrian complex, opened in 2020, that connects Asakusa to Tokyo Skytree Town via a 160-meter promenade with a glass floor viewing river traffic below. The bridge and Tokyo Skytree are lit together at night with seasonal lighting changes, and the complex includes shops and dining space along the riverbank.
records.hours: 7:00-22:00 (Sumida River Walk); individual shops keep their own hours
records.station: Asakusa Station (Tokyo Metro Ginza Line Exit 5, 7-minute walk; Tobu Skytree Line North Exit, 3-minute walk)

records.name: Sumida Park
records.description: A riverside park established in 1931 that stretches along both banks of the Sumida River, spanning Sumida and Taito wards. About 700 cherry trees planted since the Tokugawa period line the embankments, drawing large crowds in spring, and the park is a viewing spot for the Sumida River Fireworks Festival held every July.
records.station: Asakusa Station, about 5-minute walk

records.name: Asahi Beer Hall (Flamme d'Or)
records.description: The Asahi Beer Hall building on the east bank of the Sumida River, completed in 1989 and shaped like a beer glass, paired with the neighboring Asahi Group headquarters building. It is topped by the Flamme d'Or, a 360-tonne golden flame sculpture designed by Philippe Starck and built using submarine-construction techniques, symbolizing the 'burning heart' of Asahi beer.

records.name: Sumida Triphony Hall
records.description: A concert hall that opened in October 1997 and serves as the home venue of the New Japan Philharmonic. It has a 1,801-seat main auditorium and a 252-seat small hall, and its program emphasizes classical music and jazz.
records.station: Kinshicho Station (JR Sobu Line / Tokyo Metro Hanzomon Line, North Exit)

records.name: Kinshi Park
records.description: A 56,124-square-meter municipal park opened on July 18, 1928, on the site of a former Imperial Army provisions warehouse, as part of Tokyo's reconstruction after the 1923 Great Kanto Earthquake. It has baseball and tennis facilities, an indoor pool, playgrounds, and the Sumida Ward General Gymnasium, and is one of the ward's cherry blossom spots.
records.station: Kinshicho Station (JR Sobu Main Line / Tokyo Metro Hanzomon Line), about 3-minute walk from the north exit

records.name: Oyokogawa Shinsui Park
records.description: A long, narrow waterside park built along a reclaimed stretch of the Oyokogawa river in Sumida, running about 1.8 kilometers. It includes areas for children to play in the water and a fishing pond, and is listed as a neighboring facility of the Sumida Hokusai Museum.

records.name: Sumida Edo Kiriko-kan
records.description: A Sumida Ward-certified workshop and shop for Edo Kiriko, the traditional cut-glass craft that originated in 19th-century Edo. Visitors can view handcrafted glassware for sale and take hands-on cutting classes to learn the technique.
records.hours: 10:00-17:00; closed Sundays, Mondays, and year-end/New Year holidays
records.station: Kinshicho Station, about 6-minute walk

records.name: Choumeiji Temple
records.description: A Buddhist temple just north of Sumida Park on the east bank of the Sumida River. Legend holds that its well water cured the third Tokugawa shogun's back pain. The temple is historically associated with sakura mochi, the pickled-cherry-leaf rice cake said to have been created near its gate in 1717.
records.station: Oshiage Station (Skytree-mae), about 15-minute walk

records.name: Kototoi Bridge
records.description: A 237.5-meter bridge across the Sumida River connecting Asakusa with the Mukojima district, completed in 1928 on the site of the Edo-period Takeya ferry crossing. Pleasure boats pass beneath it by day, and at night Tokyo Skytree's lights reflect on the water.
records.station: Tokyo Skytree Station (Tobu Isesaki Line)

records.name: Ryogoku Bridge
records.description: A historic bridge over the Sumida River near its confluence with the Kanda River, connecting Chuo and Sumida wards. First built in 1659, its name means 'two provinces,' referring to the original crossing between Musashi and Shimosa provinces. The surrounding Ryogoku neighborhood takes its name from the bridge, which was rebuilt after the 1923 Great Kanto Earthquake and completed in its current form in 1932.
records.station: Ryogoku Station

records.name: Sumida River
records.description: A 27-kilometer river that branches from the Arakawa River in Kita ward and flows through central Tokyo, including Sumida ward, to Tokyo Bay. Around 26 bridges cross it, including Ryogoku Bridge (1932) and Azuma Bridge (1931). It has long inspired traditional art and literature, including the Noh play Sumida-gawa, and hosts the Sumida River Fireworks Festival, one of Japan's oldest firework displays, between Ryogoku and Asakusa each year.

records.name: Honjo Matsuzakacho Park (Kira Yoshinaka Residence Site)
records.description: A small park on the former site of Kira Kozukenosuke Yoshinaka's mansion, where the historic Forty-Seven Ronin carried out their revenge raid on December 14, 1701, killing Kira. The mansion had been moved here from Gofukubashi in 1701. The site was designated a Tokyo Historic Place on March 28, 1955.
records.station: Ryogoku Station (JR Sobu Line or Toei Oedo Line), 7-minute walk

records.name: Nominosukune Shrine
records.description: A small shrine near the Sumida Hokusai Museum in the Ryogoku sumo district, founded in 1884 by the first-generation Takasago stablemaster to enshrine Nomi no Sukune, traditionally regarded as the founder of sumo. Its grounds include two stone monuments inscribed with the names of successive yokozuna grand champions.
